And fords allowed them to cross in order to bring over the king’s house, and to do what was right in his sight. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, while he was crossing the Jordan.

And he said to the king, “Do not make plans against me. Mine is the guilt, my lord. And do not remember that your servant was doing wrong on the day my lord the king went into exile from Jerusalem; let not the king bear it in mind.
For your servant knows that I am guilty. And behold, I have come this day, the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”
Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered, “Should not Shimei be killed for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”

But David said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah, that you should this day be an adversary to me? Shall any one be killed in Israel this day? For do I not know that I am this day king over Israel?”
And the king said to Shimei, “You shall not die.” And the king gave him his oath.

And Mephibosheth the son of Saul came down to meet the king. He had neither bathed his feet, nor shaved his upper lip, nor washed his clothes, from the day the king went into exile until the day he came back in peace.
And when he came to Jerusalem to meet the king, the king said to him, “Why did you not go with me, Mephibosheth?”
He said, “My lord, O king, my servant deceived me, for your servant said to him, ‘I will saddle an ass for myself, that I may ride upon it and go with the king.’ For your servant is lame.
But he has said words against your servants which are unsuitable before my lord the king. But my lord the king is as wise as the angel of the LORD and must do what seems right in your sight.
For all my father’s house were but men deserving to die for my lord the king, but you set your servant among those who eat at your table. What further right of complaint have I before the king?
And the king said to him, “Why do you go on speaking your words? I say, you and Ziba shall divide the inheritance.”
And Mephibosheth said to the king, “Oh, let him take it all, now that my lord the king has come home in peace.”
Now Barzillai the Gileadite had come down from Rogelim. He crossed the Jordan with the king, to escort him over the Jordan.
Barzillai was a very aged man, eighty years old, and he had provided for the king during his dwelling in Mahanaim, for he was a very rich man.
And the king said to Barzillai, “Come over with me, and I will provide for you with me in Jerusalem.”
But Barzillai said to the king, “How many years have I still to live, that I should go up with the king to Jerusalem?

I am eighty years old. Can I discern between good and bad? Or can your servant taste what he eats or what he drinks? Or can I still listen to the sound of lutes and praise songs? Why then should your servant become another burden to my lord the king?
Your servant will go a little way over the Jordan with the king. Why should the king recompense me with such a reward?

Let your servant now return, that I may die in my own city and be buried in the grave of my father and my mother. Behold, your servant Chimham will go over with my lord the king. Do for him whatever seems right in your sight.”
And the king said, “Chimham shall go over with me, and I will do for him whatever seems right in your sight. And all that you ask of me I will do for you.”
Then all the people went over the Jordan, and the king went over. Then the king kissed Barzillai and blessed him, and he returned to his own home.
The king went on to Gilgal, and Chimham went on with him. And all the people of the House of Judah, and also half the people of Israel, brought the king on his way.

And behold, all the men of Israel came to the king and said to the king, “Why have our brethren the men of Judah held you away from us, and brought the king and the people of his house over the Jordan, and all David’s men with him?”

All the men of Judah answered the men of Israel, “Because the king is more near of kin to me than to you. Why then are you angry over this matter? Have we eaten at all from the property of the king? Or has he portioned out any gift to us?”

And the men of Israel answered the men of Judah, and said, “I have ten shares in the king. And I have more pleasure in David than you. Why then did you despise me? And was not my word to bring back my king first?” But the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.

Now there happened to be there a wicked man, whose name was Sheba, the son of Bichri, from the tribe of the House of Benjamin. And he blew the trumpet, and said, “We have no portion in David, four and we have no inheritance in Jesse’s son. Every man to his city, O Israel!”
So all the men of Israel withdrew from David to go after Sheba the son of Bichri. But the men of Judah joined their king from the Jordan to Jerusalem.

And David came to his house at Jerusalem. And the king took the ten concubine wives whom he had left to guard the house, and put them in a house under guard. And he used to provide for them, but did not go in to them. So they were guarded, and they were called until the day of their death “widows of a living husband”.
Then the king said to Amasa, “Gather before me the men of Judah within three days, and stand here yourself.”
So Amasa went to gather those of the House of Judah, but he delayed beyond the set time which he had said to him.

And David said to Abishai, “Now, Sheba the son of Bichri might do us more harm than Absalom. You must take your lord’s servants, and pursue him, lest he find himself fortified cities, and oppress us.”
And the men of Joab, and the archers and slingers, and all the heroes went out after him. They went out from Jerusalem to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

When they were at the great stone which is in Gibeon, Amasa came towards them. Now Joab was girded, wearing his clothes, and over them was a belt with a sword in its sheath girded upon his loins. And he went striding on.
And Joab said to Amasa, “Is is well with you, my brother?” And Joab took hold of Amasa’s beard with his right hand in order to kiss him.

So Amasa did not take heed of the sword which was in Joab’s [left] hand. And he struck him with it in the place of his loins, and shed his bowels to the ground – he did not need to repeat it – and he died. Then Joab and Abishai his brother pursued Sheba the son of Bichri.
And one of Joab’s men was standing by him, and said, “Whoever favours Joab, and whoever is for David, let him go after Joab.”

And Amasa lay wallowing in his blood in the middle of the road. And when the man saw that all the people stopped, he turned Amasa aside out of the road into the field, and threw clothes over him, since any one who came by saw him and stopped.
When he had turned him aside from the road, all the people went on after Joab to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.
And he passed through all the tribes of Israel to Abel and Beth maacah, and all the Berites. And they also gathered together, and came after him.
And they came and besieged him in Abel and Beth maacah. They cast up a mound against the city, and troops surrounded it. And all the men who were with Joab were planning to destroy the wall.
Then a wise woman called from the city, “Hear! Hear! Tell Joab now, ‘Draw near, that I may speak to you.’”
And he drew near to her, and the woman said, “Are you Joab?” He said, “I am.” Then she said to him, “Listen to the words of your handmaid.” And he said, “I am listening.”

And she said, saying, “I remind [you] now of what is written in the book of the law to first ask in the city! In other words, Was it not proper for you to ask in Abel, if they were willing to make peace?

We are willing to make peace in faithfulness to Israel; a city which you are seeking to destroy, that is a large fortified city and a mother in Israel. Why do you want to ruin the inheritance of the people of the LORD?
Joab answered, “Far be it, far be it from me, that I should ruin and destroy!

The matter is not so, for a man from the hill country of Ephraim, called Sheba the son of Bichri, has lifted up his hand against the king, against David. Give up him alone, and I will go away from the city.” And the woman said to Joab, “Behold, his head shall be thrown to you over the wall.”

Then the woman went to all the people in her wisdom. And they cut off the head of Sheba the son of Bichri, and threw it out to Joab. So he blew the trumpet, and they dispersed from the city, every man to his own town. And Joab returned to Jerusalem to the king.
Now Joab was appointed over all the army of Israel, and Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was appointed over the archers and the slingers.
And Adoram was appointed over the tax collectors, and Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud was appointed over the records.
Sheva was scribe, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests.
And Ira who was from Tekoa was also David’s teacher.

Now there was a famine in the days of David for three years, year after year. And David sought mercy from before the LORD, and the LORD said, “It is because of Saul and because of the house of those deserving to be killed, because he killed the Gibeonites.”

So the king called the Gibeonites and said to them – now the Gibeonites were not of the sons of Israel, but of the remnant of the Amorites; although the sons of Israel had sworn to them, Saul had sought to kill them in his zeal for the sons of Israel and Judah.
And David said to the Gibeonites, “What shall I do for you? And how shall I make expiation?” And they blessed the heritage of the people of the LORD?”
The Gibeonites said to him, “We need to receive neither silver or gold from Saul or from his house, nor a man to be killed in Israel.” And he said, “Whatever you say, I will do for you.”
They said to the king, “The man who nullified us and plotted against us – we have been stopped from dwelling in the territory of the Land of Israel –,
let seven of his sons be given to us, so that we may hang them up before the LORD at The Hill of Saul, the chosen of the LORD.” And the king said, “I will give them.”
But the king spared Mephibosheth, the son of Saul’s son Jonathan, because of the oath of the LORD which was between them, between David and Jonathan the son of Saul.

The king took the two sons of Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah, whom she bore to Saul, Armoni and Mephibosheth; and the five sons of Merab – whom Michal the daughter of Saul raised –, whom she bore to Adriel the son of Barzillai the Meholathite.

And he surrendered them into the hands of the Gibeonites, and they hanged them on the mountain before the LORD. And the seven of them fell together; they were killed in the first days of harvest, at the beginning of barley harvest.

Then Rizpah the daughter of Aiah took sackcloth, and spread it for herself on the rock, from the beginning of harvest until rain fell upon them from the heavens. And she did not allow the birds of the air to rest upon them by day, or the beasts outside by night.
When David was told what Rizpah the daugther of Aiah, the concubine of Saul, had done,

David went and took the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan from the inhabitants of Jabesh gilead, who had stolen them from the wall of Beth shan, where the Philistines had hanged them, on the day the Philistines killed Saul on Gilboa.
And he brought up from there the bones of Saul and the bones of his son Jonathan; and they gathered the bones of those who were hanged.

And they buried the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan in the land of the tribe of Benjamin in Zela, in the tomb of Kish his father; and they did all that the king commanded. And after that the LORD accepted the prayer of the inhabitants of the land.
The Philistines had war again with Israel, and David went down together with his servants, and they waged war with the Philistines. And David grew weary.
And Ishbi benob, one of the sons of the hero – whose shaft weighed three hundred selas of bronze and who was girded with a new sword belt – said to kill David.

But Abishai the son of Zeruiah came to his aid, and struck the Philistine and killed him. Then David’s men swore to him, saying, “You shall no longer go out with us to battle, for you shall not extinguish the kingship of Israel.”
After this there was again war with the Philistines at Gob. Then Sibbecai who was from Hushath killed Saph, who was one of the sons of the hero.

And there was again war with the Philistines at Gob. And David the son of Jesse, weaver of the curtains of the sanctuary, killed Goliath the Gittite, the wood of whose spear was like a weaver’s heddle rod.
And there was again war at Gath, where there was a man of stature, who had six fingers on each hand, and six toes on each foot, twenty four in number; and he also was born from the hero.
And when he taunted Israel, Jonathan the son of Shima, David’s brother, killed him.
As regards these four, they were born from the giant in Gath, and they were surrendered into the hand of David and into the hand of his servants.

And David praised in a prophetic spirit before the LORD with the words of this praise song, concerning all the days that the LORD saved Israel from the hand of all their enemies, and also David from the sword of Saul.
And he said, “The LORD is my strength and my trust and the one who rescues me.

My God, who chose me and drew me near to his fear. My strength, from before whom strength and salvation were given to me to overpower my enemies. My trust, on whose speech I trust in times of distress, shielding me against my enemies; He promised to raise my horn in his salvation. My support, whose speech was supporting me, when I was fleeing before my pursuers. My salvation from my enemies, and He saved me even from the hand of all robbers.”
And David said, “I am praying in a praise song before the LORD, who in all times saved me from my enemies.
For distress surrounded me, like a woman who sits on the birth stool, and she lacks the strength to give birth, and she is in danger of dying. A company of sinners terrified me,
armies of the wicked surrounded me, those who were armed with murder weapons confronted me.”
David said, “When I am in distress, I pray before the LORD and before my God I plea. And He accepts my prayer from his temple, my request is done before Him.
The earth was stirred and shaken, the foundations of the heavens trembled. They were bent down, because his anger was fierce.
The pride of Pharaoh went up like smoke before Him. Therefore, He sent his anger, like a burning fire which came destroying from before Him; his threat was, like coals of fire, blazing by his speech.
And He bent down the heavens and his Glory was revealed, and a dark cloud covered before Him.
And He revealed himself in his heroism upon the swift cherubim, and he rode in his strength on the wings of the wind.
He made his Presence reside in a thick cloud, a glorious cloud was all around Him, bringing down mighty waters from a mass of swift clouds in the world’s height.
From the splendour of his Glory the heavens of heavens were shining. His threat was, like coals of fire, blazing by his speech.
The LORD thundered from heaven, the Most High raised his speech.
He sent his plague like arrows, and scattered them; lightning, and confused them.
The depths of the sea were seen, and the foundations of the world were revealed, at the threat from before the LORD, from the speech of his angry strength.
A strong king sent his prophets, He who dwells in strength on high led me out, He rescued me from many nations.
He rescued me from my haters, for they overpowered me; from my enemies, for they challenged me.
They confronted me on the day of my expulsion, but the speech of the LORD was supporting me.
He brought me forth into an open place, He saved me because He chose me.”
David said, “The LORD will recompense me according to my innocence, according to the purity of my hands He will repay me.
For I kept the ways which are right before the LORD, and have not walked in wickedness before my God,
for all his judgments were revealed before me to do them, and his statutes – I did not depart from them.
I was perfect in his fear, and I was keeping my soul from guilt,
and the LORD repaid me according to my innocence, according to my purity before his speech.

Abraham, who was found loyal before Thee – therefore, Thou hast increasingly acted loyally with his seed. Isaac, who was perfect in thy fear – therefore, Thou hast perfected the speech of thy pleasure with him.

Jacob, who was walking in purity before Thee – Thou hast chosen his sons from all the peoples, Thou hast separated his seed from all the rubbish. Pharaoh and the Egyptians, who were planning plans against thy people – Thou hast confused them according to their plans.
And the people of the House of Israel, who are called ‘a poor people’ in this world, Thou wilt save, but by thy speech Thou wilt humiliate the strong, who were overpowering them.
For Thou art Master, the light of Israel is the LORD. And the LORD will bring me out of the darkness to the light, He will show me the world to come for the righteous.
For by your speech I multiply armies, by the speech of my God I subdue all strong fortified cities,
the God, whose way is straight. The law of the LORD is choice, a strength is He for all who trust upon his speech.

Therefore, on account of the miraculous salvation that Thou wilt provide for thy Anointed One and for the remnant of thy people that will remain, let all the nations, peoples and languages confess and say, ‘There is no God but the LORD, for there is no one beside Thee.’ And let thy people say, ‘There is no one who is strong, but our God.’
The God, who helps me with strength, and makes my way perfect;
making my feet as swift as the hinds, and He sets me on my stronghold;
training my hands to do battle, and strengthening my arms like a bow of bronze.
Thou hast given me strength, Thou hast saved me, and with thy speech Thou hast made me great.
Thou hast made my step great before me, and my knee did not shake.
I pursued my haters and destroyed them, and I did not turn back until I finished them.
I destroyed and finished them, so that they could not rise, the killed ones fell under the soles of my feet.
Thou hast helped me with strength to fight the battle, Thou hast scattered under me nations which rose to harm me.
Thou hast scattered before me my haters, who turned their back, my enemies, and I destroyed them.
They asked for help, but there was no saviour, and they prayed before the LORD, but their prayer was not accepted.
I trampled them like the dust of the earth, like the dirt in the streets I stepped on them; I crushed them.
Thou wilt save me from the strife of the nation. Thou wilt appoint me head of the nations; a nation that I do not know will be subjected to me.
Sons of the nations will feign to me; as soon as their ear hears, they will listen to me.
Sons of the nations will perish, and they will come trembling out of their palaces.

Therefore, on account of the miraculous salvation that Thou didst for thy people, they gave thanks and said, ‘Existing is the LORD, and blessed be the Strong One, from before Whom strength and salvation was given to us, and exalted be God, the strength of our salvation.’
The God who took vengeance for me, and scattered under me the nations that were rising to harm me.
He saved me from my haters, He made me overpower those who were rising to harm me, He will save me from Gog and the armies of the robbing nations that are with him.
Therefore, I will give thanks before Thee, O LORD, among the nations, and to thy name I will say praise.
[He who] gives great salvation with his king, and shows goodness to his Anointed One, to David and to his seed for ever.”

And these are the prophetic words of David, which he prophesied for the end of the world, for the days of consolation which are to come: David the son of Jesse said, and the saying of the man dignified to the kingdom, anointed by the Speech of Jacob’s God, and right to convey with a sweet palate the praises of Israel.
David said, “By a prophetic spirit from before the LORD I am speaking these things, and his holy words I am arranging in my mouth.”

David said, “The God of Israel spoke about me, the Strong One of Israel, Who is Ruler among the sons of men, judging the truth. He said to appoint me king, that is, the Messiah who is to rise and will rule in the fear of the LORD.

Blessed are you, righteous! You have done good deeds for yourselves, so that you are to shine in your glorious splendour, like the light of the dawn that grows brighter, and like the sun which is to shine in its glorious splendour, 343 times more in the light of the seven days. More than this you will be dignified, and it shall be good to you who are longing for the years of consolation to come. Behold, like a farmer who is hoping in dry years that rain will come down upon the land.”

David said, “More than this is my house before El, for He has established an eternal covenant for me, that my kingdom shall be lasting, as the order of creation are lasting, and secured for the world to come. Because all my needs and all my prayer are fulfilled before Him, therefore, every kingdom still opposite will not be established.

And the wicked, doing sin, resemble thorn bushes, which are in their budding soft to cut off. But when a man spares them, and leaves them, they will grow stronger, until it is impossible to approach them by hand.

And thus is every man, too, who begins to approach sins: they will grow stronger over him, until they cover, like an iron garment, him whom they could not overpower with the wood of spears and javelins. Therefore, their punishment will not be by a man’s hand, but by the fires which are to be kindled. They will be kindled in the revelation of the High Court, [which is] to sit on the throne of judgment, to judge the world.”

These are the names of the heroes who were with David, the hero, head of the armies, sitting on the throne of judgment, and all the prophets and elders surrounding him; anointed with the holy anointing oil, chosen and pampered, beautiful in looks and handsome in appearance, wise in wisdom and intelligent in council, a hero in heroism, head of the heroes; he is prepared with sets of armour, going out as the champion, and victorious in battle; and wields his spear against eight hundred slain in one time.

And next to him was Eleazar the son of Dodo, son of Ahohi, among the three heroes with David, when they defied the Philistines; and they gathered themselves there to wage war, and the men of Israel withdrew.

He rose and killed among the Philistines until his hand was weary, and his hand cleaved to the sword. And the LORD wrought a great salvation that day, and the people returned after him, only to strip the killed ones.

And next to him was Shammah, the son of Agee the Mountainite. And the Philistines gathered together at Village, where was a property of land, full of lentils; but the people fled before the Philistines.
And he took his stand in the midst of the property, and saved it. And he killed the Philistines, and the LORD wrought great salvation.

And the three heroes, from the heroes, heads of the armies, went down, and came about harvest time to David at the cave of Adullam, when the army of the Philistines was encamped in the Valley of the Heroes.
And David was then in the citadel, and the praetor of the Philistines was then at Bethlehem.
And David’s soul desired and he said, “Who would give me water to drink from the well of Bethlehem which is by the gate?”

Then the three heroes broke through the camp of the Philistines, and drew water out of the well of Bethlehem which was by the gate, and took and brought it to David. But he would not drink it, he promised to pour it out before the LORD.
He said, “Far be it for me from before the LORD, that I should do this! The blood of the men who went at risk of their lives?” So he would not drink it. These things did the three heroes.
And Abishai, the brother of Joab, the son of Zeruiah, was head of the heroes. And he wielded his spear against three hundred killed ones, and won a name beside the three heroes.
He was more renowned than the heroes, and became their commander, but he did not attain to the three.
And Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada was a man fearing sins, who did deeds, of Kabzeel. He killed the two commanders of Moab, and he went down and killed a lion in a pit on a snowy day.

And he killed an Egyptian man, a man of appearance. The Egyptian had a spear in his hand, but Benaiah went down to him with a staff, and snatched the spear out of the Egyptian’s hand, and killed him with his own spear.
These things did Benaiah the son of Jehoiada, and won a name beside the three heroes.
He was more renowned than the heroes, but he did not attain to the three heroic deeds. And David appointed him over the bodyguard.
Asahel the brother of Joab was among the heroes; Elhanan the son of Dod of Bethlehem;
Shammah, who was of Harod; Elika, who was of Harod.
Helez, who was of Palat; Ira the son of Ikkesh, who was of Tekoa;
Abiezer, who was of Anathoth; Mebunnai, who was of Hushath;
Zalmon, who was of Ahoah; Mahrai, who was of Netopha;
Heleb the son of Baanah, who was of Netopha; Ittai the son of Ribai, who was of The Hill of the sons of Benjamin;
Benaiah, who was of Pirathon; Hiddai, who was of the brooks of Gaash;
Abialbon, who was of Arbath; Azmaveth, who was of Barhum;
Eliahba, who was of Shaalbon; the sons of Jashen; Jonathan;
Shammah the Mountainite; Ahiam the son of Shara, who was from Har gaboah;
Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai the son of Maakath; Eliam the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite;
Hezrai, who was of Carmel; Paarai, who was of Arab;
Igal the son of Nathan, who was of Zobah; Banee from the tribe of Gad;
Zelek, who was from Ammon; Nahrai, who was of Beeroth, the armour bearer of Joab the son of Zeruiah;
Ira, who was of Jattir; Gareb, who was of Jattir;
Uriah the Hittite. Thirty seven heroes in all.
Again the anger of the LORD was strong against Israel, and he incited David against them, saying, “Go, count Israel and those of the House of Judah.”

So the king said to Joab, the commander of the army, who was with him, “Go now through all the tribes of Israel, from Dan to Beer sheba, and count the people, that I may know the number of the people.”

But Joab said to the king, “May the LORD your God add to the people a hundred times as many as they are, while the eyes of my lord the king still see it. But my lord the king, why does he delight in this thing?”
But the king’s word prevailed against Joab and the commanders of the army. So Joab and the commanders of the army went out before the king to count the people of Israel.
They crossed the Jordan, and began in Aroer, south of the city that is in the middle of the brook, which is in the tribe of Gad, and in Jazer.
And they came to Gilead, and to the land south of Hodshi. And they came to Dan jaan, and from there they went around to Sidon.
They entered the fortified cities, and all the cities of the Hivites and Canaanites. And they went out to the South of Judah, to Beer sheba.
So they went through all the land. At the end of nine months and twenty days they came to Jerusalem.
And Joab gave the calculation of the number of people to the king: Israel had eight hundred thousand heroic men, who drew the sword, and the men of Judah had five hundred thousand.

But David was troubled in his heart, after he had counted the people. And David said before the LORD, “I am terribly guilty in what I have done. But now, O LORD, take away the guilt of thy servant; for I have acted very foolishly.”
And when David arose in the morning, a prophetic word from before the LORD came to Gad the prophet, David’s seer, saying,
“Go and speak with David, ‘Thus says the LORD, One of three things I will impose upon you; choose one of them, that I may do it to you.’”

So Gad came to David and told him, and said to him, “Shall seven years of famine come to you in your land? Or will you be fleeing three months before your hater, while he is pursuing you? Or shall there be three days of death in your land? Now, consider and decide what I shall answer to Him who sent me.”
Then David said to Gad, “I am in great distress; let us be surrendered now into the hand of the speech of the LORD, for his mercy is great. But let me not be surrendered into the hand of man.”
So the LORD sent death among Israel, from the time that the continual offering is slaughtered until it is sacrificed. And there died from the people, from Dan to Beer sheba, seventy thousand men.

And when the angel stretched forth his hand toward Jerusalem to harm it, the LORD turned back from the evil, and said to the angel who was harming among the people, “Enough now! Stay your hand.” And the angel of the LORD was by the threshing floor of Arvan the Jebusite.

And David said before the LORD, when he saw the angel who was killing among the people. And he said, “Behold, I have sinned myself, and I have spoilt the whole thing. But these people, who are like sheep in the hand of the shepherd, what have they done? Let thy plague be against me and against my father’s house.”
And Gad came that day to David, and said to him, “Go up, rear an altar before the LORD on the threshing floor of Arvan the Jebusite.
So David went up according to Gad’s word, as the LORD had spoken.
And when Arvan looked down, he saw the king and his servants coming on toward him; and Arvan went forth, and bowed down to the king with his face to the ground.

And Arvan said, “Why has my lord the king come to his servant?” David said, “To buy the threshing floor of you, in order to build an altar before the LORD, that the epidemic may be averted from the people.”

Then Arvan said to David, “Let my lord the king take and sacrifice what seems right in his sight. See the oxen fit for the burnt offering, and the threshing sledges and the tools of the oxen for the wood.
All that the king has asked him Arvan gives to the king.” And Arvan said to the king, “May the LORD your God accept your sacrifice with pleasure.”

But the king said to Arvan, “No, for I will surely buy it from you for a price. I will not bring up burnt offerings before the LORD my God for nothing.” So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty selas.

And David built there an altar before the LORD, and brought up burnt offerings and holy sacrifices. And the LORD accepted the prayer of the inhabitants of the land, and the epidemic was averted from Israel.
versions: The Targum of Samuel; trans. E. van Staalduine-Sulman. Leiden: Brill, 2002
